haiku-low.q1: MySQL commits first. After that commit, the write copies the row to Postgres inline (flag users.dual_write). If the Postgres part fails or times out, the error is swallowed and the user's request still succeeds.
haiku-low.q2: A copy may insert a missing row, or replace a row only when its stored version is lower than the incoming version. Nothing else. A user with a tombstone is never recreated.
haiku-low.q3: Every instance reports build N, users.dual_write has been on at least 60 s, replica lag is fresh and at most 5 s, and the oldest outbox row is under 5 minutes old. Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds.
haiku-low.q4: Batches are capped at 2,000 rows with one lease holder. If replica lag exceeds 5 s or is missing, the runner sleeps 5 s and rechecks before reading the next batch.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: last compare pass clean, outbox empty, all instances on build N, then a 1%, 10%, 50%, 100% ramp, each step held at least an hour. Source of truth: 72-hour soak, clean compare, empty outbox, PG synchronous standby, verified PITR, passed rehearsal, no rollback running.
haiku-low.q6: The change is recorded in user_sync_outbox in the owner's database, written in the same transaction as the change. The row stays until the other database confirms the copy with an unchanged version. The mirror worker then repairs it.
haiku-low.q7: Tombstones: a copy never recreates a user who has a tombstone, and erase writes one in the owner's transaction. Advisory locks on the user id stop two copies of the same id running at once. Backfill also skips tombstoned ids.
haiku-low.q8: Progress (last_id) is kept in migration_backfill in PG, saved in the same transaction as the copied rows. It stops when a batch returns fewer than 2,000 rows. Batch errors stop and alert, never skip ids.
haiku-low.q9: A compare pass walks the replica in id order, comparing version and fields. Differing rows are rechecked on both primaries. Only confirmed mismatches count and are repaired through the copy function, with each pass's result written to migration_compare.
haiku-low.q10: Each database's writes check its fence row with FOR SHARE, and a freeze waits for them. A MySQL-path write re-routes once to the owner. A drain past 60 s is stopped only before step c, otherwise the MySQL owner update is retried until it succeeds.
haiku-low.q11: Before the first switch MySQL assigns ids. Each switch to PG sets the sequence to at least MySQL's counter plus 1,000,000. Each rollback sets MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT to at least the highest PG id plus 1, so ids never collide.
haiku-low.q12: PG outbox rows are copied to MySQL and a reverse compare runs continuously. Rollback: freeze PG, drain its outbox with a 60 s deadline, set MySQL's counter, flip owner and flag. The option ends at step 13, which is at least 14 days after the switch.

sonnet.q1: MySQL (primary) is written first and commits, with an outbox row in the same transaction. Then, if flag users.dual_write is on, the row is read from the MySQL primary and copied to PG (200 ms timeout). If the PG part fails or times out, the error is swallowed and the user's request still succeeds; the outbox keeps the change and the mirror worker repairs it.
sonnet.q2: Only if the incoming version is higher than the row's version (version rule: insert if missing, or replace if the existing version is lower). Also never if the user has a tombstone. updated_at is never used to decide.
sonnet.q3: Gate: every instance reports build N and users.dual_write has been on for at least two refresh intervals (60 s); replica lag is fresh and at most 5 s; oldest outbox row is under 5 minutes old. Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds after a flag change (cache refresh every 30 s).
sonnet.q4: Before each batch it checks mysql_replica_lag_seconds. If it is above 5 s or missing, it sleeps 5 s and checks again. It reads from the replica (not the primary), in batches of up to 2,000 rows (WHERE id > last_id ORDER BY id LIMIT 2000). The gate also requires lag at most 5 s before starting.
sonnet.q5: Reads to PG (step 7): last compare pass clean, outbox empty, all instances run build N; then ramp 1%, 10%, 50%, 100% with at least 1 hour per step. Source of truth (Switch 1): soak clock at least 72 hours; last compare pass clean; outbox empty; PG has a synchronous standby and verified PITR backup; step 9 staging rehearsal passed (pause at most 60 s); no rollback in progress.
sonnet.q6: The outbox row (user_sync_outbox: user_id, version, op) records it. It is kept in the owner database (MySQL in phase A), written in the same transaction as the change, and removed only when the other database confirms the copy. The mirror worker (a loop in every app instance running on table state) copies outbox rows to PG and repairs it. An alert fires if the oldest outbox row is over 5 minutes old.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones (user_tombstones: user_id, erased_at). A copy never recreates a user who has a tombstone. The backfill takes per-id advisory locks in ascending order and skips tombstoned ids inside the PG transaction; the copy function (used by backfill and repairs) enforces this. Erase writes the tombstone in the owner and the mirror writes it in the other database.
sonnet.q8: Progress (last_id) is kept in the migration_backfill row in PG (with lease owner, lease expiry, status). last_id is set in the same PG transaction as the copied rows, so a crash repeats at most one uncommitted batch. The backfill stops when a batch returns fewer than 2,000 rows, which marks it complete. A batch error (e.g. email collision) stops it and alerts, without skipping ids.
sonnet.q9: The compare pass (step 6, and continuing in the soak, plus a reverse compare in phase C). It walks the replica in id order comparing version and fields. A candidate difference is rechecked on both primaries; only a mismatch that survives the recheck counts, and it is repaired through the copy function. Each pass's result is written to migration_compare. Reads that find a row only in MySQL also count as a mismatch and queue a repair.
sonnet.q10: The fence (user_migration_state, one row per database: owner, mode, epoch). Every write begins a transaction reading its own database's fence row with FOR SHARE, so a freeze waits for in-flight writes. A frozen database returns a retryable 503; if the other database is the owner the write re-routes once. users.source is only a routing preference, so correctness does not depend on it. If the switch runs long: the drain has a 60-second deadline from the freeze; if it passes (or PG errors) before step (c), MySQL is set back to active and the switch stops. After (c) there is no going back: writes return 503 while PG is down, never falling back to MySQL, and the MySQL owner update is retried until it succeeds. Target pause is at most 90 s.
sonnet.q11: PG assigns ids, via users_id_seq. At each switch to PG the sequence is set to GREATEST(N, current) + 1,000,000, where N is MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT value. On rollback, MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT is set to GREATEST(current, PG max id + 1).
sonnet.q12: In phase C, each PG write has an outbox row in PG in the same transaction, copied to MySQL through the copy function and removed once MySQL confirms; a reverse compare (PG as reference) runs continuously. Rollback (step 12) is manual: gate is outbox empty and last reverse compare clean (run one first if none in 24 h). Then freeze PG, drain the PG outbox into MySQL (60 s deadline), set MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT, set MySQL owner mysql/active, set PG owner mysql, set users.source = mysql, mirror flips. The option ends at step 13 (phase D, at least 14 days after step 10c), when mirroring to MySQL stops and rollback is no longer possible.
